author: haiku
label: climb-07-01
changes: Added the first-run rule: pipeline_state is seeded with hwm = 1970-01-01 so the first run is a full load (Q1). Added it as an open question because the brief does not say whether one attempt can finish it.
Staging rows now carry run_date, so the start-of-attempt cleanup by run_date matches the staging schema (Q2).
Moved the committed-row check into step 0 and into the diagram as the first decision, and added the started-row-under-60-minutes rule so a crashed attempt does not block retries (Q3).
Defined run_date as the UTC date of the 02:00 start, stored on each attempt, and reused by retries and the 06:00 check (Q4).
Defined the 60-minute timeout as covering the whole attempt through COMMIT, with rollback on expiry and run_log as the resolver for a COMMIT outcome that is unknown (Q5).
Stated that the job itself pages on-call after attempt 3, and that the 06:00 alert is expected whenever no committed row exists (Q6).
Stated that the order unit is one row of orders and that child tables are not loaded, and listed child tables as an open question (Q7).
Defined the Sunday reconciliation as a step in the same job after the commit, with night_cutoff taken from that commit, and added a skipped status for reconcile_result (Q8).
Corrected the brief-conflict: the 2-hour lookback is fixed by the brief and is no longer called a proposal. Only the 60-minute timeout is a proposal.

Merged the repeated timing and failure text into one timeline table and one failure table, and moved the diagram's terms and notes to the sections around it, to cut repetition and keep the file near its original length.

Kept every stated requirement from the brief and the first version, including the 90-minute import lag, the 15-minute retries, the 30-day reconciliation window, the checksum definition, the soft-delete rule and the 06:00 alert.
Start note: a started row older than 60 minutes counts as failed, nothing rewrites it, and a job that dies sets no retry timer (Q10).
Window note: cutoff guards against writes during the extract, not replica lag (Q9).
Dedupe note: the dedupe runs in staging, before the MERGE, and why (Q12).
Sunday reconciliation note: outside the 60-minute limit and not retried; soft-deleted rows count on both sides; creation day is the UTC date of created_at on both sides (Q11, Q13).
Failure table: added a row for a reconciliation error on a day (Q11).
Failure table: added a row for a lagging replica (Q9).
Open questions: the tie-break for equal updated_at is undefined (Q12); a dead job sets no retry, so the scheduler may need one (Q10); reconciliation has no time limit or retry (Q11).
Summary cut from six sentences to three, keeping the 02:00 start, the single-transaction merge and HWM commit, and the Sunday reconciliation.
Added a terms list defining replica, warehouse, bulk import, soft delete, HWM, cutoff, lookback, attempt, run_date, run_log, staging, MERGE, creation day, checksum and on-call page.
Replaced the S0-S10 and R1-R7 step codes with plain numbered steps. Each step now says what starts it, what it does and what keeps its data.
Step 1 now states the run_date rule (UTC date of the 02:00 start, stored and reused), the 60-minute started-row check, and that a dead started row counts as failed after 60 minutes.
Step 5 now writes run_date into staging, so the next start can delete leftover rows for that date (Q2). Step 10 explains that a cleanup failure is harmless.
Step 11 and the Sunday section now state that reconciliation is a step in the same job after COMMIT, not a separate scheduler entry, and runs only when the Sunday attempt committed (Q8).

The 60-minute limit is stated as covering the whole attempt from step 1 to COMMIT, enforced by the job's own timer, with the COMMIT-timeout case resolved from run_log (Q5). Reconciliation is stated as outside that limit, with no timer and no retry (Q11).
The 06:00 check is its own section. It says the job posts the alert even when on-call was paged, and that a missing commit at 06:00 means every attempt failed or the job died (Q6).
The first-run seed (hwm = 1970-01-01, whole table loaded, no separate backfill) is kept in step 2 (Q1).
The replica-lag limit is stated plainly in the failure table: cutoff does not prevent it, the next night's lookback may catch it, and the Sunday check covers it only within 30 days (Q9).

The reconciliation section now says that soft-deleted rows count on both sides, that creation day is the UTC date of created_at on both sides, and that the reload does not move the HWM (Q13). It also says reloads are atomic per day.
The two separate failure tables and the timeline are merged into one failure table, plus a short worst-case timing table. Repeated retry and paging text is removed. Each rule is stated once.

The dedupe step and the merge rule are kept, with the equal-updated_at tie-break and the replica's one-row-per-order assumption moved to open questions (Q12). The separate Assumptions section is folded into Open questions.
Build and rollout stays as a separate section, as the first version had it.

Kept every requirement from the brief and first version: the 02:00 start, read-only replica, updated_at and soft-delete rules, the 2-hour lookback and its 90-minute reason, one row per order, HWM advancing only after load, three attempts 15 minutes apart with on-call paging, the 06:00 dashboard refresh and staleness alert, the 30-day Sunday checksum with its hash and wrapping sum, and reload on mismatch. Also kept the 60-minute and 2-hour numbers as proposals in open questions, the snapshot-isolation fallback, and the other open questions.
Added the Mermaid diagram form placed after the summary and terms, with the state table and step notes after it. The diagram itself is only lightly changed from the second version.
